editorial.titleTr: Ruling Party Escalates Standoff Over Supreme Court Justice Picks, Now Threatening to Impeach Chief Justice
summaryTr: Chief Justice Cho Hee-dae intensifies conflict by submitting Supreme Court justice nominee in writing without Blue House coordination
Democratic Party escalates political offensive beyond bounds with criticism of 'worst since liberation' and impeachment pressure
Must resolve deadlock through communication while respecting both legal procedures and established practice of consensus
editorial.bodyTr:
Chief Justice Jo Hui-dae is reporting to work at the Supreme Court in Seocho-gu, Seoul on the 19th. Yonhap News

Chief Justice Jo Hui-dae has submitted the names of Supreme Court justice candidates in writing without coordinating with the Blue House, triggering severe conflict with the ruling party. Under the Constitution, the Supreme Court justices are appointed by the president upon the National Assembly's consent, following a recommendation by the chief justice. Coordinating with the Blue House has been the customary practice in this process. The Supreme Court claims it made continuous efforts to reach an agreement but failed to do so. It appears that the Blue House's preferred candidate and Chief Justice Jo's opinion differed. Regardless of the disagreement, the decision to employ a "written notification" method without the long-standing face-to-face coordination procedure cannot escape criticism for foreclosing the possibility of amicable dialogue. Despite the court's position that it could not leave the Supreme Court vacancy unaddressed, both the Supreme Court and the Blue House should have made maximum efforts toward genuine communication and consensus-building. The Democratic Party's response, however, has overstepped bounds. Party leader Kim Min-seok used harsh language against Chief Justice Jo, calling him a "wayward student begging for expulsion" while publicly pressuring him to resign. Kim stated that Jo is "the worst chief justice since liberation" and said that if the judiciary does not acknowledge wrongdoing in this matter, all justices should voluntarily retire, and that it would be better to reorganize the Supreme Court entirely. Some lawmakers have even raised the possibility of impeachment proceedings. Threatening impeachment against the head of the judiciary while ignoring legal requirements constitutes political aggression that undermines the separation of powers and judicial independence guaranteed by the Constitution. Absent grounds for impeachment, this can only be seen as an attempt to politically pressure voluntary resignation. The solution to this crisis lies in satisfying both legal principles and customary practice for coordination. The Blue House should request the National Assembly's consent, and the National Assembly should faithfully engage in the confirmation hearing process for the nominees submitted by the chief justice. This is a matter that should be resolved by scrutinizing the qualifications of the recommended candidates within legal procedures and making a judgment on whether to approve the appointments through the National Assembly's consent process. If the National Assembly rejects the nominees, the submission process can be repeated. If the Supreme Court vacancy persists, delayed trials will ultimately harm the people. The political and judicial branches should abandon harsh rhetoric and blame-shifting, return to the spirit of the Constitution, and demonstrate the wisdom to resolve this impasse through communication.

editorial.title: Unilateral drift
editorial.body: Trump’s decision on Korea-US joint drills forces Seoul to rethink strategic posture An alliance can survive disagreement. It is harder to sustain when one side learns about a major security decision from social media. That is what happened as South Korea and the US began this year’s Ulchi Freedom Shield exercise. On Sunday, US President Donald Trump said he had ordered Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth to “substantially reduce” joint military exercises with South Korea, citing their cost and saying they send an inappropriate and hostile signal to North Korea. It is worrisome that Trump’s instruction came without any apparent advance consultation with Seoul. UFS is a defensive exercise designed to test the allies' ability to respond to a North Korean attack and strengthen combined readiness. Its value cannot be measured simply by the money spent on it. For an alliance facing a nuclear-armed adversary, training is integral to military capability. Trump's reasoning reveals a deeper structural flaw. By tying joint drills to his personal rapport with North Korean leader Kim Jong-un while publicly airing frustration over Seoul's refusal to support US efforts concerning Iran, he treats deterrence, burden sharing and out-of-area commitments as line items in a single transactional ledger. Conflating peninsular readiness with unrelated Middle Eastern conflicts undermines the predictability that collective defense requires. South Korea should take legitimate US concerns over defense costs and contributions seriously. It should also recognize that Washington has broader strategic demands. Yet collective defense requires clear boundaries. Decisions affecting combined military readiness should be reached through the institutions responsible for them, rather than announced unilaterally by a president on social media. The strategic premise behind Trump's decision is even more troubling. He described North Korea as having been "unthreatening and respectful" during his presidency. That assessment sits uneasily with Pyongyang's continued development of nuclear and missile capabilities, repeated ballistic missile launches and growing military cooperation with Russia. North Korea has gained experience and potentially useful battlefield knowledge from the war in Ukraine, including advances in precision-strike and drone warfare. Against this backdrop, reducing opportunities for US and South Korean forces to train together could create a readiness gap. It may also reinforce Pyongyang’s belief that pressure can produce results while weakening allied readiness. There is a case for diplomacy. Trump appears interested in reviving direct engagement with Kim, having met him three times during his first term. Seoul should welcome any serious opening that could reduce tensions. However, Pyongyang's strategic calculus has fundamentally shifted since 2019. Kim now has greater leverage and stronger incentives to preserve North Korea’s nuclear status, making a return to the conditions of the earlier summit diplomacy far more difficult. With the US midterm elections approaching in November, resuming diplomacy with Kim could offer the Trump administration a useful foreign-policy breakthrough that could shift public attention away from the protracted Iran war. That may explain Trump’s dramatic gesture, but it does not make the security consequences any less real. Few expect another summit between Trump and Kim to produce the concessions Washington might seek. Seoul should respond without either panic or complacency. It needs to make clear that diplomatic flexibility is possible while the core requirements of collective defense remain firm. At the same time, the Korean government should strengthen its own military capabilities and reduce vulnerabilities created by overdependence on decisions made in Washington. The Korea-US alliance remains indispensable. Its durability, however, cannot rest on personal rapport between leaders. A security partnership that can be recalibrated by a single social media post needs stronger institutional foundations. Seoul's task is to reinforce those foundations while developing sufficient independent deterrence to hedge against future shifts in Washington's strategy. 동맹은 의견 불일치로도 생존할 수 있다. 한쪽이 주요 안보 결정을 소셜미디어를 통해 알게 될 때는 지속하기가 훨씬 어렵다. 한국과 미국이 올해 을지프리덤쉴드 훈련을 시작하면서 벌어진 일이 바로 이것이다. 지난 일요일 도널드 트럼프 미국 대통령은 피트 헥스스 국방장관에게 한국과의 연합군사훈련을 "대폭 축소"하도록 지시했다고 밝혔으며, 그 이유로 훈련 비용과 북한에 대한 부적절하고 적대적인 신호라고 언급했다. 우려스러운 점은 트럼프의 지시가 서울과의 사전 협의 없이 이루어진 것처럼 보인다는 것이다. 을지프리덤쉴드는 북한의 공격에 대응할 수 있는 동맹의 능력을 테스트하고 합동 준비태세를 강화하기 위해 설계된 방어 훈련이다. 그 가치는 단순히 들어간 비용으로만 측정될 수 없다. 핵무장한 적대국과 맞서는 동맹에게 훈련은 군사 능력의 필수 요소다.

트럼프의 논거는 더 깊은 구조적 결함을 드러낸다. 연합훈련을 북한 지도자 김정은과의 개인적 친분에 연결시키면서 이란 관련 미국 노력에 대한 서울의 지원 거부에 대한 불만을 공개적으로 표출함으로써, 그는 억지력, 부담 분담, 역외 활동을 하나의 거래 원장의 라인 항목으로 취급한다. 한반도 준비태세와 무관한 중동 분쟁을 혼동하는 것은 집단방위가 요구하는 예측 가능성을 훼손한다. 한국은 국방 비용과 기여에 대한 미국의 정당한 우려를 심각하게 받아들여야 한다. 또한 워싱턴이 더 광범위한 전략적 요구를 가지고 있다는 점을 인식해야 한다. 그러나 집단방위는 명확한 경계를 필요로 한다. 합동 군사 준비태세에 영향을 미치는 결정은 그 책임을 지는 기구를 통해 도출되어야 하며, 대통령이 소셜미디어를 통해 일방적으로 발표해서는 안 된다.

트럼프의 결정 뒤에 있는 전략적 전제는 더욱 문제가 많다. 그는 북한이 자신의 재임 기간 동안 "위협이 되지 않으면서 존경스러웠다"고 묘사했다. 이 평가는 평양의 지속적인 핵과 미사일 능력 개발, 반복된 탄도미사일 발사, 그리고 러시아와의 증가하는 군사 협력과 맞지 않는다. 북한은 우크라이나 전쟁에서 경험을 얻었으며, 정밀타격과 드론 전술의 진전을 포함한 잠재적으로 유용한 전장 지식을 습득했다. 이러한 배경 속에서 미국과 한국군의 함께 훈련할 기회를 줄이는 것은 준비태세 격차를 만들 수 있다. 또한 압박이 결과를 낳을 수 있다는 평양의 믿음을 강화하면서 동맹 준비태세를 약화시킬 수도 있다.

외교의 명분은 있다. 트럼프는 첫 임기 동안 김정은을 세 번 만났던 것으로 보아 직접 대화 재개에 관심이 있어 보인다. 서울은 긴장을 완화할 수 있는 진정한 계기를 환영해야 한다. 그러나 평양의 전략적 계산은 2019년 이후 근본적으로 변했다. 김정은은 이제 더 큰 영향력을 가지고 있으며 북한의 핵 지위를 유지할 더 강한 인센티브를 가지고 있어, 초기 정상회담 외교의 조건으로 돌아가기가 훨씬 더 어렵다. 11월 미국 중간선거가 다가오면서 김정은과의 외교 재개는 트럼프 행정부에게 유용한 외교정책의 돌파구가 되어 이란 전쟁의 장기화에서 국민의 관심을 돌릴 수 있다. 이것이 트럼프의 극적인 제스처를 설명할 수 있지만, 안보 결과를 덜 현실적으로 만들지는 않는다. 트럼프와 김정은 간의 또 다른 정상회담이 워싱턴이 찾을 만한 양보를 이끌어낼 것으로 기대하는 사람은 거의 없다.

서울은 패닉도, 안일함도 없이 대응해야 한다. 외교적 유연성은 가능하면서 집단방위의 핵심 요구는 굳건하다는 점을 명확히 해야 한다. 동시에 한국 정부는 자체 군사 능력을 강화하고 워싱턴의 결정에 대한 과도한 의존으로 인한 취약점을 줄여야 한다.

한미동맹은 여전히 필수불가결하다. 그러나 그 지속력은 지도자 간의 개인적 친분에 기반할 수 없다. 소셜미디어 한 건의 글로 재조정될 수 있는 안보 파트너십은 더 강한 제도적 토대가 필요하다. 서울의 과제는 이러한 토대를 강화하면서 워싱턴 전략의 미래 변화에 대비하기 위한 충분한 독립적 억지력을 개발하는 것이다.

editorials.title: Unilateral drift
editorials.body: Trump’s decision on Korea-US joint drills forces Seoul to rethink strategic posture An alliance can survive disagreement. It is harder to sustain when one side learns about a major security decision from social media. That is what happened as South Korea and the US began this year’s Ulchi Freedom Shield exercise. On Sunday, US President Donald Trump said he had ordered Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth to “substantially reduce” joint military exercises with South Korea, citing their cost and saying they send an inappropriate and hostile signal to North Korea. It is worrisome that Trump’s instruction came without any apparent advance consultation with Seoul. UFS is a defensive exercise designed to test the allies' ability to respond to a North Korean attack and strengthen combined readiness. Its value cannot be measured simply by the money spent on it. For an alliance facing a nuclear-armed adversary, training is integral to military capability. Trump's reasoning reveals a deeper structural flaw. By tying joint drills to his personal rapport with North Korean leader Kim Jong-un while publicly airing frustration over Seoul's refusal to support US efforts concerning Iran, he treats deterrence, burden sharing and out-of-area commitments as line items in a single transactional ledger. Conflating peninsular readiness with unrelated Middle Eastern conflicts undermines the predictability that collective defense requires. South Korea should take legitimate US concerns over defense costs and contributions seriously. It should also recognize that Washington has broader strategic demands. Yet collective defense requires clear boundaries. Decisions affecting combined military readiness should be reached through the institutions responsible for them, rather than announced unilaterally by a president on social media. The strategic premise behind Trump's decision is even more troubling. He described North Korea as having been "unthreatening and respectful" during his presidency. That assessment sits uneasily with Pyongyang's continued development of nuclear and missile capabilities, repeated ballistic missile launches and growing military cooperation with Russia. North Korea has gained experience and potentially useful battlefield knowledge from the war in Ukraine, including advances in precision-strike and drone warfare. Against this backdrop, reducing opportunities for US and South Korean forces to train together could create a readiness gap. It may also reinforce Pyongyang’s belief that pressure can produce results while weakening allied readiness. There is a case for diplomacy. Trump appears interested in reviving direct engagement with Kim, having met him three times during his first term. Seoul should welcome any serious opening that could reduce tensions. However, Pyongyang's strategic calculus has fundamentally shifted since 2019. Kim now has greater leverage and stronger incentives to preserve North Korea’s nuclear status, making a return to the conditions of the earlier summit diplomacy far more difficult. With the US midterm elections approaching in November, resuming diplomacy with Kim could offer the Trump administration a useful foreign-policy breakthrough that could shift public attention away from the protracted Iran war. That may explain Trump’s dramatic gesture, but it does not make the security consequences any less real. Few expect another summit between Trump and Kim to produce the concessions Washington might seek. Seoul should respond without either panic or complacency. It needs to make clear that diplomatic flexibility is possible while the core requirements of collective defense remain firm. At the same time, the Korean government should strengthen its own military capabilities and reduce vulnerabilities created by overdependence on decisions made in Washington. The Korea-US alliance remains indispensable. Its durability, however, cannot rest on personal rapport between leaders. A security partnership that can be recalibrated by a single social media post needs stronger institutional foundations. Seoul's task is to reinforce those foundations while developing sufficient independent deterrence to hedge against future shifts in Washington's strategy. editorial.body: 조희대 대법원장이 지난 18일 이재명 대통령에게 대법관 후보로 손봉기 대구지법 부장판사와 김성수 서울고법 부장판사를 ‘서면 제청’ 하면서 헌법 정신을 무시한 독단적 행태라는 비판이 거세게 일고 있는 가운데, 19일에는 법원행정처가 노태악 전 대법관 후임 후보 추천 결과
